items.title: Treasuries, Temperament and ‘Wimpy’ Income Investing: How the Pros Say to Ride Out a Market Rout
items.summary: When tech stocks cratered and everyone ran for Treasuries, one group of retirees had already won the day. The difference had nothing to do with market timing, and a single number in your own portfolio decides which side you land on.

items.title: Fidelity and Schwab Won’t Send a Dollar of Your 401(k) RMD to Charity. The Tax-Free QCD Only Works From an IRA, and the Year You Roll Over to Get It, That Year’s RMD Can’t Move With It
items.summary: Rolling a 401(k) into an IRA unlocks the tax-free charity gift, but one year's required withdrawal gets stuck behind. Before you move a dollar, find out what that stranded payment can cost in taxes and Medicare premiums.

items.title: Anthropic partners with Plaid for AI financial advice tool
items.summary: Investing.com -- Anthropic PBC will integrate Plaid's consumer finance network into its Claude artificial intelligence model to offer personalized financial guidance to users.

items.title: Billionaires’ “Buy, Borrow, Die” Strategy Has Become A $5 Trillion Market. Here’s How It Works And What It Means For Regular Investors
items.summary: Borrowing against your stocks sounds like a loophole that lets you dodge the tax bill for good. But one clause in the lender's fine print can turn the whole plan into the very sale you were trying to avoid.

items.title: Fidelity, Schwab, and Vanguard Each Fill In a Different Beneficiary When the Line Is Blank. At One Your Kids Get It, at Another Your Estate Does, and the Difference Is Five Years to Empty It vs. Ten
items.summary: Two widowed parents leave the same $600,000 IRA to their kids without ever naming a beneficiary. One family gets room to plan, the other gets a probate filing and a tax clock. A single clause in your custodian's fine print decides which.
